title: GroupBy Aggregation That Proves Itself
objective: After this lesson you will be able to aggregate sales by category/country/month with named aggregations, pivot for reports, resample time series, and reconcile every total back to raw counts.
why: 'Revenue by category' drives pricing, inventory, and marketing — and wrong totals drive them off cliffs. Aggregation bugs (fanout joins, NaN groups, double-counted dupes) hide inside plausible numbers. Reconciliation (grouped totals sum to grand totals sum to raw) plus named aggregations plus resampling discipline make every number traceable to rows.

blocks.text: Named aggregation (`agg(total=('price','sum'), orders=('id','count'))`) produces self-documenting columns — no MultiIndex riddles, no positional guessing. One verb per question: sums for money, counts for volume, means with n alongside (means without counts mislead on tiny groups — always pair them).

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
csv = "cat,price\nshoes,129\nshoes,139\napparel,59\nshoes,100\n"
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv))
r = df.groupby("cat").agg(total=("price", "sum"), n=("price", "size")).reset_index()
print(r.to_dict("records"))
print("reconciled:", float(r["total"].sum()) == float(df["price"].sum()))

blocks.text: Pivot for reports, resample for time

**pivot_table** reshapes long-to-wide for readable reports (categories × months with margins=True checksumming). **resample** buckets datetimes (ME month-ends, W weeks) after setting a DatetimeIndex — irregular series become regular, missing periods explicit (fill or flag, never silently skip). Both end with reconciliation: margins sum, periods counted.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
csv = "day,amount\n2026-09-05,100\n2026-09-20,150\n2026-10-03,200\n"
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv), parse_dates=["day"])
m = df.set_index("day").resample("ME")["amount"].sum()
print(m.to_dict())
print("months:", len(m), "total:", float(m.sum()))

blocks.text: Three reconciliations, every aggregation: grouped sums = grand total = raw sum (fanout/dupes break this first); group counts sum to row count (NaN keys vanish — decide fill vs drop explicitly); pivot margins match groupby totals (reshape fidelity). Failed reconciliation names the bug class: fanout (joins), NaN groups, or duplicates.

blocks.title: Aggregate and reconcile
blocks.note: Run it: expect shoes 368, apparel 59, reconciled true, grand 427. Grouped sums equal raw sums — the invariant every aggregation in this lesson must satisfy.

items: Named aggregations (self-documenting) with means always paired with n
Pivots with margins, resamples with explicit missing-period policy
Triple reconciliation (grouped = grand = raw) names fanout/NaN/dupe bugs on failure

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice aggregator and confirm shoes/apparel/reconciliation/grand. (b) In Python, replicate with groupby + named agg on the same four rows; assert reconciled. (c) Break it deliberately (duplicate one row pre-aggregation) and state which reconciliation fails and what it diagnoses.
hints: Python: groupby('cat').agg(total=('price','sum')) then sum-vs-raw assert (must hold).
Duplicated row inflates one group: grouped still sums to (inflated) grand, but grand ≠ trusted raw — reconciliation against the cleaned baseline diagnoses duplication.
exercise.why: Twin parity (JS mirrors pandas), assert-driven aggregation (reconcile in code, not by eye), and breakage diagnosis (which invariant fails names the bug) are the three aggregation disciplines.
exercise.code: # Reconciliation asserts: grouped.sum() == raw.sum() — in code, every time.

quiz.q: Grouped totals exceed raw sum. First suspects in order?
options: Join fanout, then duplicates, then double-counted NaN handling — reconcile staged counts to isolate
quiz.explain: Inflation has three usual causes in order: fanout multiplies, dupes double, NaN mishandling shifts. Staged counts isolate which.

quiz.q: Mean without n per group. Problem?
options: Tiny groups mislead: mean of 2 vs mean of 2000 need n alongside — always pair
quiz.explain: Unweighted means hide sample size: pair every mean with its n, and distrust small-n cells explicitly.

quiz.q: Resampled months skip empty periods silently. Fix?
options: Explicit missing-period policy (fill with 0/NaN + flag, or drop with note) — silent gaps misread as zero-activity or break joins
quiz.explain: Missing periods are information (no sales vs unrecorded). Policy stated, gaps flagged — never silently absent.

summary: Named aggregations with n, pivots with margins, resamples with explicit gaps, triple reconciliation always. Numbers traceable to rows or they don't ship.
next: Aggregated honestly — now enrich: joins with cardinality guards and as-of features without leakage. Next: merging without multiplying.
